subject: multilevel model with ARMA(1,1) within each group can't converge, BFMI is low

messages.author: 0b079035c63442d8
messages.subject: multilevel model with ARMA(1,1) within each group can't converge, BFMI is low
parts:
Dear all stan users,

I am working on a multilevel model now, each group has different number of observations, arma(1,1) is applied within each group. In the result, n_eff is 1, Rhat is about 1e+14 for almost parameters. The warning message is like this:

[1] "The following numerical problems occured the indicated number of times on chain 2"
                                                                                         count
Exception thrown at line 30: normal_log: Location parameter is inf, but must be finite!    647
Exception thrown at line 30: normal_log: Location parameter is -inf, but must be finite!   244
[1] "When a numerical problem occurs, the Hamiltonian proposal gets rejected."
[1] "See http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#exception-hamiltonian-proposal-rejected"
[1] "If the number in the 'count' column is small,  do not ask about this message on stan-users."
                 ^
Warning messages:
1: There were 2 chains where the estimated Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information was low. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bfmi-low 
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

any suggestion for this issue? Thanks a lot


here is the code:
data{
  int<lower=1> N;       // number of observations
  int<lower=1> J;       // number of groups (engines)
  vector[N] y;          // observed response
  vector[N] x;          // observed predictor
  int<lower=1, upper=J> jj[N]; // group indicator
  int npereng[J];              // number of observations by group
}
parameters{
  real mu_a;
  real mu_b;
  vector[J] a;             // intercept for each group
  vector[J] b;             // slope for each group
  real<lower=0> sigma_y;   // erro term for response
  real<lower=0> sigma_a;   // error term for intercept
  real<lower=0> sigma_b;   // error term for slope
  vector[J] phi;                // autoregression coeff
  vector[J] theta;              // moving avg coeff
}
model{
  real error;
  int sn;
  phi ~ normal(0, 2);
  theta ~ normal(0, 2);
  sigma_y ~ gamma(3, 1);
  sigma_a ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  sigma_b ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  mu_a ~ normal(0, 100);
  mu_b ~ normal(0, 100);
 
  a ~ normal(mu_a, sigma_a);
  b ~ normal(mu_b, sigma_b);
 
  sn = 0;
  for (j in 1:J) {
    error = y[sn+1] - a[j] - b[j]*x[sn+1];
    for (n in 2:npereng[j]) {
      y[sn+n] ~ normal(a[j] + b[j]*x[sn+n] + phi[j]*y[sn+n-1] + theta[j]*error, sigma_y);
      error = y[sn+n] - a[j] - b[j]*x[sn+n] - phi[j]*y[sn+n-1] - theta[j]*error;
    }
    sn = sn + npereng[j];
  }
}

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: multilevel model with ARMA(1,1) within each group can't converge, BFMI is low
parts:
Not exactly sure what is happening but you may want to try the brms R package (based on Stan), which allows for ARMA models within groups.
You can also just let brms write you the Stan code and amend it if needed.

parts:
Thank you Paul, I tried brms like this:

fitarma <- brm(AP21VIBE ~ CYCLES + (1 + CYCLES | ENG_SN), family=gaussian, prior=c(prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b"), prior(normal(0, 2), class="Intercept")), cor_arma(~CYCLES | ENG_SN, p=1, q=1), data=ap21, iter = 1000, chains = 2)


and got one phi / theta value for whole dataset, but what I thought is that there should have different phi/theta values for different groups.

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: Re: multilevel model with ARMA(1,1) within each group can't converge, BFMI is low
parts: The ctsem R package specifies and fits this sort of model using Stan. See the package and hierarchical vignette on CRAN, (more extensive article pre-print also on my researchgate), and in particular the sunspots example in the vignette - this is a carma(2,1) model, but you can change the ctModel function to specify a discrete instead of continuous time model, and figure out how to change the model matrices as needed. Maybe it helps.
